notes: F3 solver model: drainage allowance frozen at 30 mm/h [P] (2026-11-26); 20 of 20 named runs finished. Calibrated on the city's two current-sea-level maps (limited 1.77 in/h, moderate 2.13 in/h); the 3.66 in/h run is a check against a 2080 map. Every number comes from the run folders, the city maps and the cache files listed as inputs. Captions: calibration_curve.png: Modelled area per city class (4 in to 1 ft, 1 ft and over) on the compared cells against the drainage allowance, one marker per calibration run, with the city map's area as a dashed line; below, the critical success index for wet (4 in or more) with model patches under a quarter acre removed (filtered) and without (raw), and for the deep class; green: the frozen value. Limit: 12 runs, each 1 h of uniform rain on the whole square; the city's maps come from another model, so a match is agreement with that model, not with observed flooding. hit_miss.png: Hit, miss and false alarm per compared cell at the frozen allowance, wet meaning 4 in or more, model patches under a quarter acre removed; grey: compared and dry in both; white: not compared (outside the study area, under a building footprint, a filled pit or water). Limit: a cell takes the city's class at its centre; a shift of one cell between the two maps counts as both a miss and a false alarm. water_balance.png: Rain, drained (the allowance), stored (change in water volume) and out (net outflow through the four edge cross-sections) per run, thousand m³, over the cells inside the boundary cells; the residual share of the rain is printed above. Limit: the fluxes are the solver's own outputs, so the balance tests their consistency, not that the rain or the drainage are right. replays.png: Peak depth at cell centres for each replay on the compared cells of the study area, in three classes; red: substation sites with the depth exceeded on 25 m² of their open ground; right: the radar rain each run was forced with, mean over the 4 km square per step. Limit: radar rain at about 1 km cells, held uniform within each cell and hour; no sewer network, only the allowance; water from outside the square cannot enter. atlas14.png: NOAA Atlas 14 60-minute depth at the study-area centre against return period, partial duration and annual maximum series, with their 90% bounds, and the three map intensities held for one hour. Limit: a point estimate for a 4 km area; the city's storm shape and duration are not a 60-minute block, so a placement is a reading, not the return period of the map. sensitivity.png: Change in modelled area at 4 in or more (filtered) and in CSI wet against the frozen run of the same scenario, for other durations at the same intensity and other boundary levels. Limit: one run per setting, at the frozen allowance only.

frozen.note: Limited alone fits best near 30 mm/h, Moderate alone between 30 and 35 mm/h. CSI (wet) at 30 mm/h is below the proposed 0.5 on both maps; accepted by Yuri as the best fit, to be stated on the page. No official sewer-district layer was found, so the per-district fallback of FH3 was not tried.
frozen.objective: Smallest sum, over the Limited (1.77 in/hr) and Moderate (2.13 in/hr) current-sea-level maps, of the squared log ratio of modelled to city area in each class (4 in to 1 ft; 1 ft and over), on compared cells (study-area land outside footprints, pits, water and cells below the start water level), after the model's wet patches under a quarter acre are removed. Allowances tried: 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 50 mm/h. One-hour storm at the stated intensity [P], one dry hour after.
